defects.description: Plan builds a new offset-based inbox cursor (src/lib/inboxCursor.ts, OFFSET query) instead of the shared keyset helper in src/lib/pagination.ts. Offset paging duplicates/skips rows when new notifications arrive (violates AC1) and departs from the existing list convention.
Plan caps limit at 100; spec R1/AC2 require limits above 50 to be treated as 50.
markRead updates by notification id only, with no user_id filter, so any authenticated user can mark another user's notification read (violates R2/AC4).
defects.location: plan.md steps 2 and 6; spec.md R2, AC4

defects.description: The UPDATE includes `AND read_at IS NULL` and the handler returns 404 when rowCount is 0, so marking an already-read notification returns 404, contradicting R2/AC3 (idempotent 204).
Test strategy has no test for cross-user access (AC4), for repeat mark-read (AC3), or for paging stability under inserts (AC1); the mocked-pool tests cannot detect the missing user filter.
defects.location: plan.md test strategy; spec.md AC1, AC3, AC4

defects.description: R4 (POST /v1/notifications/read-all) and AC5 are not implemented; the plan defers mark-all-read to a later release.
defects.location: plan.md rollout notes; spec.md R4, AC5

tensions.description: Architecture's natural fix is to reuse parseLimit/decodeCursor/toPage from src/lib/pagination.ts. But parseLimit clamps to the module constant MAX_LIMIT = 100 with no per-endpoint option, so reusing it as-is keeps the 100 cap that consistency wants changed to 50. The obvious alternative for consistency (set the cap to 50) would mean editing a shared constant used by every list endpoint. Visible only in the fixture helper.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Delete inboxCursor.ts and use the shared keyset pagination helper (parseLimit, decodeCursor, toPage).
tensions.lens_b_fix: Cap limit at 50 for the inbox as R1 requires.
tensions.reconciliation: Reuse the shared helper but give parseLimit an optional max argument (defaulting to MAX_LIMIT so the activity feed and other callers are unchanged) and pass 50 from the inbox route; add a test for both caps.

tensions.description: Risk's natural fix adds `AND user_id = $2` and keeps 'rowCount 0 means 404' so other users' notifications are not found. Consistency's natural fix for idempotency is to stop treating rowCount 0 as an error (return 204). With the `read_at IS NULL` guard still in place, the two cannot both hold: rowCount 0 means either 'already read' or 'not yours/not found', and one fix breaks the other's AC.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Filter the UPDATE by user_id and return 404 when no row matches.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Return 204 when no row is updated, so repeat calls are idempotent.
tensions.reconciliation: Drop the read_at IS NULL predicate and use `SET read_at = COALESCE(read_at, now()) WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2`: rowCount 0 now means only 'not found or not owned' (404), while an already-read row still matches and keeps its first read_at (204). Test AC3 and AC4 explicitly.
